messages.subject: error in createCel
parts:
Hi,

I am running analysis of Mouse Exon arrays. I have created a custom cdf
(long story) and am fitting the plm model. I have actually done this
before but am rerunning it (including making the custom cdf) to make
sure I didn't have an error in what I was doing. In order to do this, I
moved away from my 'standard' aroma.affymetrix directory and made a new
one with Windows shortcuts to my annotationData and rawData files. I
have rerun the BC and QN and have rerun a plm fit on one custom cdf with
no problem. However, I am getting an error when I try to run the plm on
the next custom cdf. The new custom cdf is the same (but name) from the
old, as best I can tell (see below). But I am getting an error in the
fit function from createCel when it creates blank cels for storing the
effects. Any ideas? (I've tried deleting everything including the
.RCache and the monocell.cdf file and trying it again).

Thanks,
Elizabeth

Here's my test that the new cdf is the same as the old cdf (which ran
fine with this same code up to different names...).
> LowHuIndices80Pct<-getCellIndices(cdfMoEnsb50_Filter80PctJt_HM)

[1] 14990

[1] 14990
> length(unlist(LowHuIndices80Pct))
[1] 152543
> length(unlist(LowHuIndices80PctOld))
[1] 152543
> all(unlist(LowHuIndices80PctOld) %in% unlist(LowHuIndices80Pct))
[1] TRUE

This is the code I am running:
cdfMoEnsb50_Filter80PctJt_HM<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipTypeMo,tags=c("U-Ensembl50","G-Affy","customMH","joint","80PctLowHu","80PctHighMo","EP"))

plmMoOnMo_Filt80PctJt_HM <- ExonRmaPlm(csNMoOnMo_HM,
mergeGroups=TRUE,tags=c("*","ensb50NOv","customMH","joint","80PctLowHu","80PctHighMo"))
#if mergeGroups==FALSE, then each exon separately
fit(plmMoOnMo_Filt80PctJt_HM, verbose=verbose)

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] error in createCel
parts:
Hi,

this has nothing to do with the new CDF nor the Windows Shortcut
links, but instead a Windows specific limit of the length of the
absolute path/pathname you are trying to create. Yours are too long.

Your current directory is:

rootPath <- "C:/Documents and Settings/Elizabeth/My
Documents/Research/ExonArrays/aroma.affymetrix.work/MouseHuman/Filter_80PctJt";

The output directory is:

outPath <- "plmData/MouseHuman,RBC,QN,MoOnly,RMA,merged,ensb50NOv,customMH,joint,80PctLowHu,80PctHighMo/MoEx-1_0-st-v1";

The filename is:

filename <- "MO1-4 C9_(MoEx-1_0-st-v1),chipEffects.CEL";

The complete pathname is:

path <- file.path(rootPath, outPath);
mkdir(path);
stopifnot(isDirectory(path));
pathname <- file.path(path, filename);
print(nchar(pathname));
[1] 265

FYI, if you have a relative pathname, you can do pathname <-
getAbsolutePath(pathname) to get the full pathname.

I don't know the exact limit of the pathname, but it is around 255 or
so. The easiest in your case is to shorten the length of 'rootPath'.
Personally, I would also drop '(MoEx-1_0-st-v1)'. If you don't want
to/cannot rename the original CEL files in the rawData/, you can use
so called name translators to change the filenames. See Vignette
'Empirical probe-signal densities and rank-based quantile
normalization' for an example how to do the latter:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/empirical-probe-signal-densities-and-rank-based-quantile-normalization

If you don't mind, could you please do a few examples on pathname of
different lengths and see when file() gives an error or not, and then
report to r-devel. This could simply be due to a bug/overseen limit
in R rather than Windows with an easy fix.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: error in createCel
parts:
Hi,

I stumbled on a solution/workaround for Windows. With the command
'subst' you can assign a device letter to any pathname. In your case,
you can do something like:

# Mount drive letter X: to long path

cmd <- sprintf('subst X: "%s"', rootPath);
system(cmd);

Now, have start R with X:/ as the working directory, instead of
"C:/Documents...". Similarly, you can have Windows Shortcuts to point
to such mounted devices.

# Unmount drive letter X:
system("subst X: /D");

/Henrik
